sherwood_ranger.text: Welcome to the Visitor Centre. The Major Oak is a short walk away, and about a thousand years old. Maybe eight hundred. It does not give interviews.
It is named after Major Hayman Rooke, who wrote about it in 1790. It is propped up with supports, and weighs about 23 tonnes.
This forest holds one of the biggest collections of ancient oaks in Europe. Over 900 veteran trees. I know a few of them by name.

then.text: You already have my snare. Do not make me weave another before lunch.

else.text: Here, take a snare. Wicker, hand woven, entirely legal. Be gentle with whatever you catch.

sherwood_volunteer.text: Barkdeer yaps at the first sign of strangers. If you hear one, you are probably being announced.
Fawnlet hides in the bracken all day. Mum comes back at dusk, so do not fuss it. The barnling hunts by sound, so keep your voice down.

else.text: Every acorn off the Major Oak is spoken for. Except the odd one I polish up for friends.
Hazelnuts round it for luck, and a truffle from under the old roots. It makes whoever holds it stand like an oak.
Pop in whenever you've got the makings. You can use my kitchen.
